page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.2xlarge is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor operating at 2.7 GHz. Built on x86_64 architecture, the configuration provides 8 dedicated virtual CPUs across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The host offers 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a 1:2 RAM-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU core. CPU cache hardware includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of shared L3 cache. Supported hardware extensions include AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES, VAES, SHA_NI, BMI2, and FMA instructions. The instance features no local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes, and operates with a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth under KVM hypervisor management.

Benchmark results demonstrate consistent mid-tier compute efficiency across general workload categories. The instance achieved 1886.99 in single-core stress-ng tests and 7766.94 in multi-core CPU evaluations. Memory bandwidth measurements reached 56.88 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 38.8 GB/sec for uncached writes. In application benchmarks, the instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 5889.0, a software compilation rating of 8136.0, and 7.95 million Redis SET operations per second. However, performance degrades on memory-intensive generative AI models, placing in the bottom 10% for 7B parameter LLM prompt processing at 16.13 tokens per second.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM balance and dedicated Intel Xeon cores, the ecs.c7t.2xlarge offers cost-effective execution for CPU-dominated workloads that do not require high memory density or bundled local NVMe storage. Primary suitable workloads include static web serving, software compilation pipelines, microservice backends, CI/CD execution, and lightweight database nodes.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c7t.2xlarge is a compute-focused virtual instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical Intel Xeon 8369B cores clocked at 2.7 GHz. Equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per vCPU) and a 48 MB L3 cache, it supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 VNNI and AES cryptography. The server relies entirely on external network storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps. Synthetic benchmarks place its general compute, memory bandwidth, and database performance in the middle 50th percentile, reaching 7766.94 in stress-ng multi-core tests and 7.95 million Redis SET operations per second. Hardware throughput degrades on memory-heavy tasks such as 7B parameter LLM execution. The system offers solid qualitative efficiency for CPU-bound tasks, including software compilation, web serving, microservices, and light database operations.
